3 REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Description The material powder. shall be in the form of grey brown comply with the 5.2 BIS Certification Marking

The product may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Sta'ndard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 6 SAMPLING Representative samples of the material shall be drawn according to IS 10946. 7 QUALITY OF REAGENTS

3.2 The material shall also requirements given in Table 1. 4 PACKING

The material shall be packed in mild steel drum, HDPE or fibreboard drums with polyethylene liner of thickness not less than 0.123 mm. It shall also conform to the general requirements given in IS 8190 (Part 1). 5 MARKING 5.1 The drums shall be marked legibly and indelibly with the following information: a) b) c) d) Name of the material; Name and address of the manufacturer; Batch'No. or Code No.; Date of expiry; 1

DETERMINATION A-O GENERAL A-0.1 Either of the two methods namely, UV Spectrophotometric method (see A-l) or HPLC method (see A-2) may be used for determination of thiophanate methyl content. However, in case of dispute, HPLC method will be the referee method. A-l A-l.1 UV SPECTROSCOPIC Principle METHOD

A-1.4.2 Preparation of Developing Solvent-Mix 45 parts of ethyl acetate with 4 parts of methanol and 5 1 parts of n-hexane by volume. A-1.4.3
Preparation of Chromatography Column

The sample of thiophanate methyl is purified by passing through a silica gel column. Absorbance of the sample solution at 269 mm is compared with that of the standard of known purity to determine the content of thiophanate methyl. A-l.2 A-1.2.1
A-1.2.2

Apparatus
UV Spectrophotometer

Pour into the column a slurry made from 6 g of silica gel and 20 ml of developing solvent. Drain the solvent by applying pressure of nitrogen gas till the level is just above that of the silica gel column. Wash down any silica gel sticking to the walls of the column by carefully washing down with the developing solvent so as not to disturb the silica gel column. Again drain the solvent so that its level is just above the silica gel by applying pressure of nitrogen gas. A-1.4.4
Preparation of Sample Solution

Weigh accurately into a 50 ml volumetric flask a sample equivalent to about 175 mg thiophanate methyl. Add 40 ml of ethylacetate and keep it for one hour at 70�C with frequent shaking. Cool the solution to room temperature and dilute up to the mark with ethylacetate. A-1.4.5

A-1.3.5 Silica Gel-Column 200 mesh particle size. A-l.4 Procedure

A-1.4.1 Standard Preparation Weigh accurately 100 mg of standard thiophanate methyl of known purity into a 100 ml volumetric flask, dissolve in methanol and dilute to mark with methanol. Pipette out 10 ml of this solution into a 100 ml volumetric flask and make up to mark with methanol. Pipette out 10 ml of this solution into a 100 ml volumetric flask, add 7 ml developing sofvent (see A-1.4.2) and make up the volume up to mark with methanol.
NOTE-Analytical reference of thiophanate methyl having purity more than 99 percent should be used. This can be prepared

To the chromatography column prepared as in A-1.4.3 add carefully 5 ml of the sample solution (prepared in A-1.4.4) by means of a long tipped dropper. Wash the walls of the column twice with 1.5 ml of the developing solvent. Finally add 40 ml of the developing solvent without disturbing the silica gel bed and apply nitrogen pressure so that a flow rate of 2 ml/minute is maintained. Collect the elute in a 50 ml volumetric flask till the solvent level in the column is just above the silica gel bed. Make up to mark with developing solvent. Again pipette out 10 ml of this solution in a 50 ml volumetric flask and make up to mark with the developing solvent. A-1.4.6
Determination

Transfer 7 ml of the eluate obtained in A-1.4.5 to a 100 ml volumetric flask and dilute up to mark with methanol. Compare the absorbance of this solution with that of the standard solution (as prepared in A-1.4.1) at 269 nm. A-1.5 Calculation mt x A2 xPxZ Thiophanate methyl content, = m2 x AI percent by mass

A-2 HPLCMETHOD A-2.1 Principle

qf Sumple Solution

A HPLC unit, equipped with a UV detector, is used for this assay. The solution of thiophanate methyl is compared with that of standard thiophanate methyl of known purity by using HPLC at 269 nm. A-2.2 Apparatus Liquid Chromatogruph

A-2.2.1 High Pr@rmance

A high performance liquid chromatograph equipped with a printerplotter-cum-integrator and UV detector. The suggestive HPLC operating conditions are given below. However, these operating conditions can be varied provided standardization is done. Column : Lichrosorb RP-8, 10 pm, 25 cm x 0.46 cm, stainless steel or other equivalent column Acetonitrile: Methanol: Water 1: I:2 by volume 2Opl

Weigh accurately a sample equivalent to about 125 mg thiophanate methyl into a 250 ml volumetric flask. Add 200 ml methanol and dissolve the sample. Make up to volume with methanol and mix thoroughly. Transfer by pipette 5.0 ml of this solution into a 50 ml volumetric flask. Add by pipette 5.0 ml of internal standard solution (A-2.4.1). Make up to mark with mobile phase and mix thoroughly. A-2.5 Estimation

Introduce 20 ~1 of standard solution (A-2.4.1) into the HPLC system followed by sample solution (A-2.4.2). Note the areas of the thiophanate methyl and internal standard peaks. Calculate the thiophanate methyl content. A-2.6 Calculation
